title: Check an import function
prompt: `ImportCandidates` is supplied. Write `public static bool CheckImport(Func<List<string>, ImportReport> candidate)`. Return true for both correct import functions. Return false for the candidates that group names case-sensitively, ignore rejected-row counts, or drop valid zero-count keys. Use inputs that expose all three mistakes. Also make sure a candidate leaves its input list unchanged and handles an empty list. Test the candidate's behavior only. Do not inspect source text or use reflection.
hints: Use fresh input lists for the candidate calls. Include names whose spelling differs only by case and include a valid zero count.
Add malformed, empty-name, negative, overflow and extra-field rows. Check the exact rejected count and make sure invalid rows do not become keys.
Check the exact totals through differently cased lookups, verify the zero key exists, compare the input with a copy, and call the candidate with an empty list.
checkLabels: Your check must accept a correct loop-based import function.
Your check must also accept a different correct import function.
Your check must reject case-sensitive grouping of Ada and ada.
Your check must reject a function that does not report invalid rows.
Your check must reject a function that drops a valid zero-count key.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Accepts every candidate without testing it.
Rejects correct candidates along with faulty ones.
Checks one sample total but never checks invalid rows or zero counts.

feedback: Make your check distinguish behavior that looks similar in a small happy-path sample. Cover casing, invalid-row counts, zero keys, and empty input.
